summary: Sudden 5xx wave during connection pruning after tenant traffic shift
description:
Issue summary: Around 2026-03-13 02:12 UTC we observed a sudden, sustained increase in 5xx responses (primarily 502/503) for a subset of Intellibook traffic in us-east-1. The error pattern presents as a sawtooth: short spikes of elevated 5xx over a 2–3 hour window, correlated with connection pruning events on edge proxies and aggressive keepalive trimming from the autoscaler when a tenant shift occurred.

Impact: Intellibook reported timeouts and degraded throughput for interactive chat endpoints. Estimated 25–35% of their requests that touch redwood-2.0 experienced transient failures; customer business impact: reduced availability for their live editor sessions. Only dedicated-tier tenant traffic observed; other tenants unaffected.

Environment: prod-us-east (us-east-1), affected pool: dedicated-gpu-pool-12, ingress layer: edge-apigw-v4, runtime pool: redwood-runtime-ssd-12.

Timeline (UTC):
- 02:08: autoscaler triggered a tenant shift (traffic moved from pool-12 to pool-8 for capacity balancing).
- 02:12: first 502s observed in Intellibook traces; Grafana shows accept-queue depth drop and connection pruning spikes.
- 02:14: Keepalive metrics show abrupt drop in active keepalive sessions on edge-apigw-v4.
- 02:20: Runtime pods start reporting short-lived OOM-adj warnings and increased latency; connection resets observed in proxy logs.
- 04:30: manual mitigation applied (disable aggressive connection pruning; bump keepalive window), error rates return to baseline by ~04:45.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Simulate tenant traffic shift (move 30–50% of tenant sessions from one dedicated pool to another) while running streaming chat sessions with long-lived connections.
2) Trigger autoscaler policy that performs connection pruning/route rebalancing.
3) Observe 502/503 spikes and accept queue fluctuations in ingress metrics.

Observed logs/metrics:
- Grafana dashboard: apigw.accept_queue.length spiked then collapsed; apigw.conn_prune.count increased from 0 to >120/min during bursts.
- Sample proxy log lines (edge-apigw-v4):
  "[2026-03-13T02:13:21Z] WARN conn_prune: pruning 18 keepalives for tenant intellibook (pool-12 -> pool-8)"
  "[2026-03-13T02:13:22Z] ERROR upstream: read reset by peer (downstream conn closed) status=502 request_id=..."
- Runtime logs: short-lived kv-cache lock warnings and GC feedback loops; no full runtime process crashes but transient evictions and increased latency.

Initial hypothesis: The autoscaler connection-pruning logic aggressively trimmed keepalive pools during a tenant shift, causing sudden mass connection resets. The edge API gateway then retried requests which amplified load on the target runtime pods; a subset of runtimes hit memory pressure/GC spikes (not full OOM kills) and returned 502/503. Downstreams amplified due to short retry policy and insufficient backlog headroom at the runtime side.

Temporary mitigation applied:
- Disabled aggressive conn-pruning for pool-12 at 02:22 UTC.
- Increased keepalive window on edge-apigw-v4 from 60s to 180s for Intellibook routes.
- Applied a soft cap on concurrent prefetch threads for the affected runtime pool.
Result: 5xx spike subsided within ~20 minutes; customer traffic restored.

Resolution (work in progress): Root cause appears to be an interaction between the new autoscaler pruning algorithm and the edge keepalive reuse heuristics under rapid tenant shifts. A permanent fix will require:
- Autoscaler change to perform staggered pruning with backoff and health checks.
- API gateway change to drain keepalives more gracefully and avoid immediate retries that amplify pressure.
- Runtime tuning to increase accept queue headroom during tenant rebalances.

Follow-ups: Create a postmortem, coordinate code changes across infra (autoscaler) and edge (apigw), and schedule a controlled test of tenant-shift scenarios in staging with canarying.
steps_to_reproduce: See description timeline. Quick repro: in staging, shift ~40% of sessions off a warmed pool while running long-lived streaming sessions; enable conn-prune policy; watch apigw.accept_queue and apigw.conn_prune metrics.
observed_metrics: apigw.accept_queue.length: dropped from 120->10 during pruning; apigw.conn_prune.count: spike to >120/min; runtime.latency.p95 increased 2x; 5xx-rate for intellibook endpoints rose from 0.4% to ~28% during window.
investigation_notes:
- Correlated timestamps between apigw logs and runtime traces show pruning events precede 502s by ~1-3s.
- No evidence of kernel OOMs or node reboots.
- Autoscaler logs show prune job started as part of 'pool consolidation' routine after utilization metric crossed threshold.
- Linked INT-4210 contains earlier discussion about pruning algorithm concerns.
- Related PR https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/8362 contains a change to pruning heuristics introduced two weeks ago.
mitigation: Applied immediate config changes (disabled aggressive pruning, bumped keepalive), and temporarily exempted Intellibook from pool consolidation until the autoscaler fix ships.
next_steps: 1) Owner: infra-autoscaler team to implement staggered pruning + health checks (PR referenced). 2) Edge team to add graceful-drain and retry-backoff for keepalive resets. 3) Runtime team to increase accept-queue reserve for dedicated pools during rebalances. 4) Run staged chaos test: tenant-shift scenario in staging. 5) Draft postmortem and publish to Confluence.
customer_communication: Initial: Acknowledge receipt and explain we identified a correlation between our autoscaler connection-pruning and elevated 502/503s during a tenant shift. We applied mitigations to restore availability and will follow up with root cause and timeline. ETA for permanent fix: 5 business days. (Communicated 2026-03-13 03:10 UTC by CS).
